Die Beurteilung der Eignung der Bieter erfolgt anhand der mit dem Angebot eingereichten Erklärungen und Nachweise ( Kriterienkatalog Eignung und Teil E) . Fehlende Erklärungen und Nachweise werden einmalig nachgefordert. Die Verfristung einer Nachforderung führt zum Ausschluss des Angebots. Zur Feststellung der Eignung ist mindestens eine vergleichbare Referenz aus den letzten angegebenen Geschäftsjahren gefordert (E4). Zuverlässigkeit sowie wirtschaftliche und finanzielle Leistungsfähigkeit (z.B. Umsatzzahlen, Gesamtmitarbeiterzahl) müssen vom Bieter oder der Bietergemeinschaft oder unter Zuhilfenahme eines Unterauftragnehmers (Eignungsleihe) nachgewiesen werden (E1). Angaben von Bietergemeinschaften werden dabei addiert. certifications_partner.text: erhöht. Konfiguration SSL Um SSL zu aktivieren, wird die benötigte Konfiguration in der Datei /etc/httpd/conf.d/ssl.conf vorgenommen. Zusätzlich müssen ein Zertifikat und eine Zertifikat-Key-Datei auf den dort angegebenen Verzeichnissen abgelegt werden. 2024 wurde das neue Zertifikat als .pfx Datei geliefert. Aus einer pfx-Datei können die benötigten Zertifikate mit folgendem Befehlen erstellt werden: Schlüssel als pem extrahieren: $ openssl pkcs12 -in <PFX_file> -nocerts -nodes -out verwaltungsportal1_key.pem RSA Key nochmal nach .key konvertieren openssl rsa -in verwaltungsportal1_key.pem -out verwaltungsportal1.key Public Certificate extrahieren: $ openssl pkcs12 -in <PFX_file> -clcerts -nokeys -out verwaltungsportal_cert.crt CA Chain extrahieren: $ openssl pkcs12 -in <PFX_file> -cacerts -nokeys -chain verwaltungsportal_ca.crt Die Dateien müssen auf den Server übertragen werden und ersetzen folgende Dateien: (definiert sind diese in /etc/httpd/conf.d/ssl.conf) • SSLCertificateFile /etc/pki/tls/certs/verwaltungsportal.crt • SSLCertificateKeyFile /etc/pki/tls/private/verwaltungsportal1.key • SSLCACertificateFile /etc/pki/tls/certs/verwaltungsportal-ca.crt Nach Überschreiben reload der Konfiguration. 4.3.5 Konfiguration SSO Für die Installation des Singl

(MVVM) development pattern, where you would have to code the presentation layer by creating View Models and Views for each object you wish to display, using NOF there is only a set of default generic (MVVM) views defined by NOF and they are applied to all domain objects (models). The Naked Objects pattern was first described formally in Richard Pawson's PhD thesis which includes a thorough investigation of various antecedents and inspirations for the pattern including, for example, the Morphic user interface. Naked Objects is commonly contrasted with the model-view-controller pattern. However, the published version of Pawson's thesis (see References) contains a foreword by Trygve Reenskaug, who first formulated the model-view-controller pattern, suggesting that Naked Objects is closer to the original intent of model-view-controller than many of the subsequent interpretations and implementations. Further information on the NO pattern is available at http://www.nakedobjects.org/ . Naked Objects 2.0 The BOMi currently uses version 2.0 of the Naked Objects framework, referred to as 'NOF2', which was the first publicly available framework to implement the 'naked objects pattern'. NOF2 was originally written by Naked Objects Group and supplied to the Department under an open-source licence.

Reference No.: TZ-EAC-564358-CS-CQS

1. BACKGROUND

The East African Community (EAC) Secretariat is implementing the EAC component of the Eastern Africa Regional Statistics Program-for-Results (EARSPforR), with financing from the World Bank. The Program seeks to strengthen the production, harmonization, dissemination, and use of quality economic and social statistics in Eastern Africa.

Under EARSPforR, the EAC Secretariat has developed online learning materials in fourteen priority statistical domains for use by Partner State institutions and other data users. Although technically sound, many of the materials are text-heavy an

. The videos will incorporate infographics, accurate data visualizations, professional voice-over narration, captions, and transcripts, and will be suitable for the EAC Learning Management System, websites, and mobile access.

To support this mission, the Government requires a modern software solution that serves as a relational database and analysis toolset. This toolset is essential for the iSMART (interoperable Systems Management and Requirements Transformation) process and is used to populate, edit, analyze, and manage TDL message data, platform implementations, and interoperability evaluations. 2.0 SCOPE The Contractor shall provide a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software solution, including all necessary licenses, updates, training, and technical support. The software shall provide a comprehensive toolset for managing TDL platform specifications, conducting interoperability analysis, and supporting mission planning across the TDL enterprise. 3.0 REQUIREMENTS The Contractor shall provide the following: 3.1 Software Capabilities The provided software solution shall mee

When preparing a competitive quotation, vendors should take into consideration benefits provided through the national healthcare system. Quotations should refrain from over customization, and should be “off the shelf”, “commercially available”, or “market ready” products which are designed to be complementary and supplement to the national system in Portugal. The benefit levels listed from section C.1.1 through C.1.24 are a standard package that must be provided. C.1.1 Eligibility: To be eligible to participate in the medical plan, LE Staff (both full time and part time) must be: -- Paid under the terms of the Local Compensation Plan (LCP); and – -- Under a non-temporary direct hire appointment, personal services agreement (PSA), or personal services contract (PSC); or -- Under a temporary direct hire appointment or PSA Fixed Term of one year or more. Not eligible are those working under temporary appointments; those working under a PSC or PSA that is time limited to less than one year; non-personal services contract personnel and their employees, supplied by an independent contractor l

ointments; those working under a PSC or PSA that is time limited to less than one year; non-personal services contract personnel and their employees, supplied by an independent contractor licensed to do business in Portugal who provides services to other local RFP 19GE5026Q0035 – LES Health Insurance Services for U.S. Embassy Lisbon Page 6 of 21 organizations as well as to the U.S. Mission; employees working on an intermittent or When Actually Employed (WAE) schedule; Peace Corps personal services contractors and Recreation Association employees. C.1.2 Riders: There are no riders under this contract. C.1.3 Periods of Ineligibility: Employees and their dependents are not entitled to health benefits during any period of employment for which premiums are not paid. Additionally, employee's dependents are not entitled to health benefits during any period of employment during which the employee was not eligible to participate. During a period of extended Leave Without Pay (LWOP) or other unpaid leave beyond one pay period, the employee is responsible for the full cost of the insurance premiums for self and dependents. The Mission will pay the premiums directly to the Contractor and will collect the full cost from the employee on a quarterly basis. Alternatively

GENERAL The U.S. Government requires Health and Life Insurance for its Locally Employed Staff (LES) of the United States Embassy Lisbon, Portugal and their eligible dependents as described herein. The Contractor shall provide health insurance services under this contract to eligible employees at U.S. Embassy Lisbon and U.S. Consulate Ponta Delgada, Azores. TYPE OF CONTRACT 1. This is a fixed-price indefinite delivery/indefinite quantity (IDIQ) with economic price adjustment requirement under which annual firm-fixed price task orders will be issued. The fixed premium rates for the health insurance services as specified in Section C – Statement of Work provided herein are provided in Attachment 3 – Pricing Schedule. The quantities set forth in the pricing section are estimates; the Government does not guarantee that such quantities will be ordered. 2. The contract will be for a one base year period and four (4) one-year periods. In accordance with FAR 52.217-8, the contract may be extended by additional six (6) months period. Services shall commence no later than January 01, 2027. The Government is obligated only to the extent of authorized task orders actually made under this IDIQ. 3. Payments will be made only to the extent specifically authorized in the task order. Each task order will fund a specific period of time and number of covered individuals. ACQUISITION METHOD This is a commercial acquisition as defined in the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 2.101, Definitions, and as described in FAR part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. STATEMENT OF WORK C. 1. OVERVIEW/BACKGROUND. The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory

The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory of NLS DA2 devices. NLS requires quantities suffi
